item.title: After Week of Turmoil at Cornell, a Heavy Cloud Hangs Over Student Life
item.description: As the weekend arrived, much of the nightlife in the upstate New York college town was subdued. But there were still some students looking to cut loose.
item.dc:creator: Maia Coleman
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: Students and patrons outside bars and restaurants on Friday night in Ithaca, N.Y., home to Cornell. Many said they couldn’t remember a weekend on campus this quiet.

item.title: A Campus Reckoning: ‘Cornell Is Now Known for This’
item.description: Accusations of sexual assault at a fraternity party have tarnished the self-image of a fiercely proud Ivy League institution. Can the university ever be the same?
item.dc:creator: John Leland and Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: On the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., the rituals of a new school year have been replaced with a reassessment of what it means to be a student there.

item.title: Tariffs Are Making Instruments So Expensive, School Music Programs Are at Risk
item.description: When a single cello can cost $1,000 and a tuba $9,000, tariffs are straining meager band and orchestra budgets.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:description: Many schools rely on inexpensive beginner instruments that are made largely in China.

item.title: Why Are France’s Students Protesting?
item.description: Demonstrations for a better-funded education system have led to blockaded schools, thousands of arrests and a national political reckoning.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel and Zane Irwin
item.media:credit: Tom Nicholson/Getty Images
item.media:description: Students demonstrating in Paris on Wednesday.

item.title: How Cornell Punished Each of the 7 Men Accused of Sexual Assault
item.description: Summaries obtained by The New York Times offer a detailed look at the discipline meted out to the men accused of sexually assaulting a fellow student at Cornell University.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman, Hurubie Meko and Debra Kamin
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Of the seven fraternity members accused of assaulting Jane Doe at a Cornell University fraternity house, two were expelled, two were suspended and the other three received lesser punishments.

item.title: Teen Charged With Attempted Murder and Domestic Terrorism After Chemical Spill
item.description: The 15-year-old mixed and ingested hazardous chemicals at a school cafeteria in Portland, Ore., last month, officials said. His lawyers denied the allegations.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin

item.title: Cornell Case Revives Anger About Handling of Campus Sexual Assault Cases
item.description: A lawsuit alleging rape at Cornell has led to an outpouring of women sharing stories about sexual violence on college campuses.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Saul and Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: On the campus of Cornell University and beyond, women are talking about their own experiences of sexual assault.

item.title: How a Cornell Student Went From Shame to Action
item.description: The woman known as “Jane Doe” was initially embarrassed about what happened at a fraternity party in 2024, but soon concluded: “I was assaulted.”
item.dc:creator: Debra Kamin, Matt Flegenheimer, Amy Julia Harris and Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Prosecutors have reopened the case of a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity brothers in 2024.

item.title: U.C.L.A. Says Justice Department is ‘Weaponizing’ Civil Rights Laws
item.description: The fiery language came months after the Justice Department accused the university of abetting antisemitism against students.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Alisha Jucevic for The New York Times
item.media:description: The University of California, Los Angeles, says it has made efforts to protect Jewish and Israeli students, contrary to the government’s claims.

item.title: Statement Written by Police in Cornell Assault Case Omitted Her Claim She Was Raped
item.description: Documents obtained by The New York Times show that the campus police at Cornell University sent a condensed statement to a prosecutor, who then declined to bring charges.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Police Department summarized hours of interviews with a woman who said she was raped into a six-page document that excluded key details. A local prosecutor did not pursue criminal charges based on that document.

item.title: American University of Afghanistan at Risk of Closure Amid Funding Cuts
item.description: The State Department has denied its funding for the next two years, jeopardizing the education of hundreds of female Afghan students.
item.dc:creator: Elian Peltier, Yaqoob Akbary and Safiullah Padshah
item.category: United States Agency for International Development
item.media:credit: Kiana Hayeri for The New York Times
item.media:description: A graduation ceremony at the American University of Afghanistan in Kabul in 2019.

item.title: As Cornell Reckons with Sexual Assault Case, Will Applicants Think Twice?
item.description: Many alumni and some prospective parents are rethinking their relationships with Cornell. But as one admissions consultant said, “Prestige is a powerful draw.”
item.dc:creator: Troy Closson
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University has been rocked by a woman’s explosive lawsuit accusing several men of raping her at a fraternity house.

item.title: How Parents Are Talking to Sons About the Cornell Rape Allegations
item.description: At the dinner table and during school commutes, families are navigating difficult conversations with their sons about sexual assault and moral responsibility.
item.dc:creator: Christina Caron and Catherine Pearson
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times

item.title: Cornell Students Call for Change at Fiery Public Meeting
item.description: Through tears, some students shared stories of assaults they had experienced, while others spoke out to criticize administrators and demand improved training on consent.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Emma Goldberg/The New York Times
item.media:description: At a public forum at Cornell’s student union, some students expressed rage at the way a rape allegation was handled.

item.title: The School Near Paris That Shows Why French Students Are Protesting

item.title: Need Help Paying for College? Try Bass Fishing.
item.description: The popularity of competitive bass fishing has inspired a growing number of youth, high school and college fishing programs.
item.dc:creator: Ken Belson and William DeShazer

item.title: Sally Yates to Lead Internal Investigation Into Cornell’s Handling of Sexual Assault Report
